author: ValWood
body:
Right I see SGD has made this annotation from 
[retrograde transport, endosome to Golgi](https://www.yeastgenome.org/go/GO:0042147) ([IGI] [SFT2](https://www.yeastgenome.org/locus/S000000198)(http://wiki.geneontology.org/index.php/Inferred_from_Genetic_Interaction_(IGI)))

from
https://www.yeastgenome.org/reference/S000040382
Got1p and Sft2p: membrane proteins involved in traffic to the Golgi complex. EMBO J 18(14):3934-46

but the abstract says
Thus the presence of either [Got1p](https://www.yeastgenome.org/locus/S000004906) or [Sft2p](https://www.yeastgenome.org/locus/S000000198) is required for vesicle fusion with the Golgi complex in vivo. We suggest that [Got1p](https://www.yeastgenome.org/locus/S000004906) normally facilitates Sed5p-dependent fusion events, while [Sft2p](https://www.yeastgenome.org/locus/S000000198) performs a related function in the late Golgi.

so this is inferred from defects in a double mutant  (SFT2 GOT1) which operate in differnet pathways.
Got5  is  implciated in a common pathway with sed5.
However sed5 is not known  to be part of  retrograde transport, endosome to Golgi.
is is ER to Golgi
https://www.yeastgenome.org/locus/S000004016

So I don't believe this annotation is necessarily correct.

Also the SGD description for Got1 says

Homodimeric protein that is packaged into COPII vesicles; cycles between the ER and Golgi; involved in secretory transport but not directly required for aspects of transport assayed in vitro; may influence membrane composition [1](https://www.yeastgenome.org/locus/S000004906#reference) [2](https://www.yeastgenome.org/locus/S000004906#reference)

Taken together I would remove this mapping.

author: ValWood
body:
a later paper says

PMID: 19383723

Further characterization of Got1p revealed that this protein was efficiently packaged into COPII vesicles and cycled rapidly between the ER and Golgi compartments. Based on the findings we propose that Got1p has an unexpected role in vesicle formation from the ER by influencing membrane properties.

so based on this  it is not shown to have a direct role in transport although it does cycle between these compartments.
